summary.name: Incident response, programs and you(r startup)
summary.one_liner: A long-form essay by Will Larson on how company incident response evolves from ad-hoc on-call to a formal incident program, proactive reliability work, and centralized SRE teams as a startup scales.
keywords: how to run incidents at a startup
use_cases: Planning how a startup should formalize incident response as it grows
Setting up an incident training and roles structure
Deciding whether to create a centralized SRE team
Prioritizing reliability work across many incidents
summary.what_it_does: The essay walks through stages a company passes through in handling incidents: an ad-hoc shared on-call rotation, a formal incident program with training, tooling, defined incident roles and incident review, and a shift to proactive reliability investment. It describes an investment thesis, bulk incident management, reliable architecture and quality assertions as ingredients for prioritizing reliability work. It also discusses the tradeoffs of centralized SRE response teams. The author gives rough organization-size thresholds based on his experience, such as around 200 and 500 engineers, and names Blameless as similar to internal tooling many companies build. It is an opinion piece drawn from the author's experience rather than a tool with features.
notable: Describes the progression from ad-hoc on-call to formal incident program to proactive reliability
Argues incident programs should shift from owning a process to owning a product
Discusses downsides of centralized SRE teams for accountability and novel incidents
Listed under the On-Call section of dastergon/awesome-sre
caveats: Opinion essay based on the author's experience; organization-size thresholds are rough guidance, not rules
Does not cover a specific software product's features or pricing
